01 · Complete product coverage

Every page has an implementation.

The source contains nine chapters: six product studies and three review or handoff documents. The six studies describe 11 distinct page designs across 15 primary route patterns. The review chapters informed the work and the decisions below.

#PageImplemented behavior
01HomeSix scenarios; contest-first hero, live board and current-user standing. Join, register, log, retry and recap actions lead to real local flows.
02Profile overviewYear controls update score, entries, activity calendar, languages, contest history and recent activity together. Profile links retain identity and contest context.
03Activity logSearch plus year, language and activity filters; removable chips, result counts and recovery from no matches. Entries open their own detail records.
04Admin workspaceDistinct admin shell, responsive sidebar and seven working sections. Content editors and report review update local collections and queues.
05About TadokuEditorial introduction, the shared immersion promise, practical examples and contextual routes into the guide and contests.
06Start hereA readable manual covering joining, logging, personal tracking and contest participation, with contextual actions and all three navigation proposals.
07Scoring & rulesPersonal and contest score contexts explained with worked examples, Reading/Listening terminology, eligibility and ended-round behavior.
08Questions & helpSix complete searchable answers; accessible keyboard disclosures, answer search, no-match recovery and local contact handoff.
09LeaderboardLatest, yearly, all-time and individual-contest scopes. Filters recalculate rank; name search preserves it. Pagination and Find my row move to and focus the actual row.
10ContestsOfficial, Community and My contests collections; dates, registration deadlines, status, discovery filters and owner controls. Unlisted contests remain accessible by link.
11Log detailsSeven states. Personal activity, contest contributions and frozen scores are distinct. Owners can edit, manage submissions, delete and restore; visitors see the public record.

Supporting flows also built

Contest details, contest standings, registration, organizer create/edit, log create/edit, sample sign-in with return destination, account settings, contact draft and not-found recovery.

Admin sections: Posts, Pages, Announcements, Languages, Contests, Users and Reports. Local content editors and moderation actions provide usable feedback.

These are additional routes and forms, rather than extra master-page designs counted in the eleven.

A connected journey, with shared state

  1. Join from Home
    Guest sign-in retains the intended contest.
  2. Register languages
    Eligibility and selection limits use field validation.
  3. Log & edit activity
    Amounts, dates and per-contest scores stay distinct.
  4. See the result
    Home, profile, activity and standings reflect the saved record.
  5. Delete & restore
    Confirmation, Escape, focus and score changes are exercised.

The browser verified Home’s score round trip of 600 → 1,100 → 600 and confirmed Leaderboard also showed 1,100 after adding the same activity. A separate journey saved 12 points, edited the same record to 14, found Anton at 614 points, and followed the record through activity history.

02 · Beyond the happy path

Lifecycle, permissions and empty states.

StudyCoverageDetails worth inspecting
Home · 6Guest live; member not joined; participant live; upcoming; between rounds; unavailable.Join versus log actions, registration deadlines, current-user standing, recap and recovery. Between-round links retain their sample date.
Leaderboard · 9Participant; guest; member; registration closed; closed participant; upcoming; ended; empty; unavailable.Three main scopes plus contest-specific boards, tied ranks and zero scores. Language/activity filtering changes rank; name search does not.
Contests · 6Member; guest; between rounds; no organized contests; organizer; unavailable.My contests means organized contests. Joining and logging use different eligibility gates. Unlisted entries are excluded from public discovery.
Log · 7Reading; listening; visitor; personal only; ended contest; missing; unavailable.Owner-only submissions are hidden from visitors. Reading and listening can have different contest rates. Later personal edits preserve closed snapshots.
Profile & shellOverview, activity and admin; owner/visitor and empty activity; years 2023–2026.The selected year drives every summary. Mobile navigation and filtered recovery work.
GuideFour pages × three information-architecture options.B · Guide plus About is the default. A · four familiar pages and C · task-based help remain selectable in Playground controls.

The sample baseline is 5 September 2026, UTC. Lifecycle scenarios use their own explicit dates. Data identities are shared across pages; inconsistent literals from the source studies were normalized into a usable sample dataset. Yearly and all-time standings use illustrative fixture multipliers with local score adjustments; their baselines are not sums of the displayed historical activity. Real aggregate queries remain part of production integration.

03 · Changes promoted into Paper

Real pages found four shared gaps.

Problem exposed by a pageShared changeEvidence
“Find my row” had no row target.Table.getRowProps now accepts native row attributes. Consumers can supply an ID, tabIndex, aria-current and presentation while keeping links and buttons inside native table cells.Regression verifies forwarded attributes and focus. The leaderboard changes page and focuses Anton’s actual row; the guide has an executable focus example.
Autocomplete could not express eligibility.Single and multiple autocomplete now accept RHF rules, including custom validation and messages. Tags inherit the same contract.Single/multi validation regressions; registration language limits; guide example requires two selections and displays a meaningful recovery message.
Escape erased selected values.Paper cancels Base UI’s Escape-driven value/input clearing. Escape dismisses the popup and preserves the selection, including after the popup has unmounted.Failing single/multi regressions reproduced the timing issue. Browser registration retained Japanese after closing, waiting and pressing Escape again.
Neighboring hints stretched form controls.Field grid content aligns to the start; hints follow controls so adjacent inputs share a baseline. Native date/time segment padding no longer adds a second inset.Mixed-hint inputs previously measured about 56.3px/47.8px; now both ordinary and date fields measure exactly 44px comfortable / 36px compact. The canonical Input example includes this arrangement.

Page composition and behavior refined alongside the package

  • The mobile header keeps Log activity on one line and switches the account trigger to an accessible icon menu. Long names were checked from 320px through 1440px.
  • Selecting a scenario establishes its account for the pages that follow it. Direct organizer navigation stays on the requested contest collection.
  • Registration, logging and leaderboard filters use coherent language choices. Date context follows lifecycle actions through create, detail and edit. Existing log language and activity stay fixed, as specified in the master.
  • Personal scores and contest submissions use explicit, separate sample calculations. Missing required tracked time and unregistered languages block the relevant contest submissions; personal logging remains available. Ended submissions retain their saved scores.
  • Home totals use saved/deleted submissions; profile sections use one selected-year dataset. Profile overview/activity links retain identity, year and contest context; yearly standings link to the matching profile year.
  • Organizer fields align to a shared edge; page sections use Paper typography, flat surfaces and restrained rails. Tables retain a deliberate scroll region at narrow widths.

These product rules and page arrangements remain in the playground. The four reusable component fixes are in paper-ui and documented through the same source files the styleguide renders.

04 · The preceding styleguide work

Normal Tailwind utilities, clearer usage.

The comprehensive Paper review and utility setup were merged in PR #857 (main merge 2825052e). Its full 44-page review ledger remains available.

Use familiar class names

// tailwind.config.cjs
module.exports = {
  presets: [require('paper-ui/tailwind-preset')],
  content: ['./src/**/*.{ts,tsx}'],
}

// In a page
<Surface className="p-4 md:p-6">
  <div className="flex gap-2">…</div>
</Surface>

p-4, gap-2 and responsive variants use Paper’s scale through the preset. Semantic utilities include bg-paper, text-ink and border-rule. gap-inline and min-h-control follow density.

The preset overrides Paper’s named spacing stops while retaining the rest of Tailwind. Paper supplies the reset. Standalone Paper component CSS remains usable without Tailwind.

Feedback addressed

  • Single setup page; explicit class/prop references before implementation variables.
  • Color table with one role per row, plus useful spacing, density, layout, accent-rail and elevation demonstrations.
  • Source-backed rendered examples and syntax-highlighted code, with readable API and accessibility sections.
  • Preview theme isolation, contained demo links and route scroll reset.
  • Correct violet segment in the light wordmark.
  • Action-menu trigger choices including chevron and icon-only ellipsis, with accessible labels.

This iteration adds realistic Table, Input and Autocomplete examples and documents the new contracts. It does not introduce a parallel set of playground-only buttons or form controls.

05 · Verification and its limits

What was actually checked.

GateResult
Automated behaviorPaper: 201 tests in 31 files. Styleguide: 141 tests in 21 files. Playground: 41 tests in 6 files. Boundary checker: 3 tests. All passed.
Public package contract49 copyable source examples compile against published exports; TypeScript 4.9 consumer check passes; 36 package files validated; legacy/Paper import boundaries pass.
Build and static checksFull pnpm build passed for all six frontend apps and their package dependencies. Paper, styleguide and playground typechecks pass. Lint has zero errors.
132 layout/state casesHome/Guide 42; leaderboard/contests 30; profile/log/admin 44; supporting forms 16. Desktop and 390px, light/comfortable and dark/compact coverage. No unintended document overflow or JavaScript errors in the checked cases.
Browser interactionsJoin/sign-in/registration; ranking, filtering, paging and row focus; organizer create/edit; profile year and filters; log edit/submissions/delete/restore; FAQ keyboard search; admin Drawer/review/editors; contact draft and settings.
Regression measurementsMixed-hint/date controls 44px/36px; header one-line action at five widths; preserved autocomplete selections after closed-popup Escape; Home’s score round trip and the board’s updated total were verified.

Browser automation used actual Chromium and the built Paper package. This is not a Safari/Firefox or screen-reader certification. The committed ledgers retain case-level outcomes, and screenshots show the rendered pages rather than the source HTML mockups.

Non-blocking tool output remains: eight Fast Refresh warnings from colocated playground helper exports, one existing styleguide RHF compiler warning, and Vite’s 500kB chunk warning. The playground’s main JS chunk is about 558kB minified / 182kB gzip before production optimization. Font and bundle budgets belong in the next production integration pass.

Evidence directory: source-inventory.json, records-browser.json, contests-browser.json, evidence/editorial-browser.json, journey-browser.json, supporting-browser.json and focused reproduction scripts.

07 · Run and review

A separate place to keep refining Paper.

The app lives at frontend/apps/paper-playground. Its quality workflow checks imports, lint, types, tests and build. The workflow has no image build, publishing or deployment step.

cd frontend
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm paper-playground

Open Playground controls in the footer to switch page, scenario, account, theme, density or help navigation. Reset sample changes restores the fixtures. Log, registration and settings changes stay in browser storage. Administrative editor changes stay in the mounted local workspace; the contact form prepares an unsent draft.

Temporary private preview

https://t3-0ef85f6d4b774f389dc36a46.lab
Session 0ef85f6d4b774f389dc36a46 · verified HTTP 200.

The link requires private lab or tailnet reachability, .lab DNS and Lab CA trust. It has no application authentication and serves only sample data.

When finished with the preview: t3-expose stop 0ef85f6d4b774f389dc36a46.

The work followed the published implementation plan: merge the existing system, implement the source pages in parallel, fix shared defects from real usage, and retain a durable report and evidence.

08 · Collected for our next review

Decisions still worth making together.

These choices were kept open while implementation continued. None requires undoing the page studies.

01 · Help navigation

Confirm Home’s priority and the help navigation.

Current choices: a contest-first Home and B, Guide plus About. The homepage hierarchy is a proposal from the source, not an approved or measured conversion improvement. Review whether contest participation should lead for each audience. All four help pages also work under A’s separate pages and C’s task-based labels; compare the three with Playground controls.

02 · Scoring and timing

Approve production rules and saved provenance.

The sample demonstrates different personal and contest rates, registration eligibility and frozen ended scores. Confirm repeated material, playback speed, media rules, late edits, moderation and submission windows. The eventual service needs to retain the rule used for each saved contribution so historical totals remain explainable.

03 · Service contracts

Keep the working journeys when connecting real data.

Define server-authoritative membership and organizer/admin permissions; organized-contest discovery and unlisted visibility; scoped ranking, name search and current-user row retrieval; filtered profile summaries and log ownership. Replace sample sign-in and local mutations when those contracts exist.

Two product choices remain explicit: should joined contests have a separate collection alongside My contests (organized), and should visitors ever see a log’s contest contributions? The current implementation keeps My contests as organized and hides owner-only contribution details.

04 · Fonts and delivery

Set a font policy and performance budget.

Latin Paper fonts are bundled. CJK samples were checked with an available system fallback, but the shipped app does not bundle that fallback. Choose the languages to guarantee, canonical language identifiers and display labels (including Chinese/Mandarin), font subsets or system policy, and minimum wordmark size. Measure the real application’s bundle and font load before selecting further splitting or subsetting work.

The next useful step is to review these page journeys, settle the decisions above, and connect one complete path to real APIs. The same playground can remain a place to reproduce future Paper defects with realistic content.
